title: Define ensemble prompt-sampling strategy and actionable regression triggers for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Optimize needs a deterministic, actionable eval and gating system so that model/quantization changes do not cause silent regressions in production. Current ad-hoc prompt sets and single-threshold rollbacks generate noisy alerts and frequent manual investigations.

Goal: Deliver a PRD that defines (1) an ensemble prompt-sampling matrix that represents real production traffic and edge cases, (2) multi-signal regression thresholds with tiered actions, (3) A/B evaluation criteria & minimum detectable effect (MDE) guidance, and (4) a practical rollback/playbook mapping signals to actions (canary rollback, stop rollout, escalate to AI SRE).

This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, and an initial operational runbook for integration with the Console and Optimize pipelines.
scope:
In scope: prompt sampling strategy design, quantitative regression signal definitions, A/B statistical test spec, threshold-to-action mapping, runbook text for automated gating. Integration touchpoints: Optimize evaluation pipeline, Console alerting, and rollout controller.
Out of scope: implementation of model-serving kernel changes and full automation of rollback execution (will be tracked in ENG sub-issues).
success_metrics: Reduction in false-positive eval alerts by >= 50% in first month; average time-to-detection of true regressions <= 30 minutes for canary traffic; zero customer-facing quality incidents attributable to Optimize rollouts in the quarter.
prompt_sampling_plan: Use an ensemble sampling matrix consisting of: (a) traffic-proportional sample (70%) drawn from production logs with stratified sampling across routes/models; (b) edge-case buckets (20%) aggregated from customer-reported prompts and historical failure modes (long context, nested JSON, multimodal markers); (c) adversarial/rare scenarios (10%) seeded from internal fuzzing suites. Maintain a living prompt catalog in Drive and tag prompts with metadata: route, expected_token_count_bucket, semantic_category, safety_flag. Sampling update cadence: weekly for traffic-proportional set, monthly for edge-case expansion.
regression_thresholds: Define multi-signal thresholds: (1) Core quality signal: metric = weighted composite of prompt-set accuracy (or pass-rate on structured outputs), and n-gram similarity/embedding-based drift; soft-warning at 1.5% relative drop, hard-fail at 4% relative drop. (2) Latency signal: p95 latency increase > 25% triggers review, > 50% triggers abort. (3) Safety degradation: any uptick in safety classifier false-negative rate > 0.2% OR >= 1 high-severity safety slip in canary triggers immediate stop. (4) Cost/per-token signal: sustained > 30% unit cost increase triggers manual approval. Thresholds tied to MDE and historical variance—use rolling 28-day baseline and require sustained deviation for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (window = daily hourly-binned batches) before hard action.
ab_test_spec: A/B framework must support: sample size calc using pre-specified MDE (default 1.5% absolute for core quality signal), control:current allocation 80/20 for canary runs, statistical tests: two-sided permutation test with bootstrap CI for composite metrics; adjust for multiple comparisons using Benjamini-Hochberg when evaluating >1 metric. Required pre-registration of hypotheses in Confluence. Stopping rules: early stop for futility if projected MDE unattainable given observed variance after 48 hours; mandatory manual review for any significant safety signal even if other metrics pass.
rollback_playbook: Tiered actions mapped to signals: (A) Soft-warning (investigate): notify PM/AI SRE/Responsible owner; pause rollout growth; increase sampling frequency. (B) Canary-fail (stop and rollback): automatic rollback to previous model variant if core quality hard-fail OR safety hard-fail observed in canary population. (C) Escalation (manual intervention): if multi-signal mixed failures or customer-impacting signals present, open incident with SEV classification and block further deployments until RCA. Playbook includes exact runbook steps (notification templates, dashboards to check, PR/commit IDs to revert), and links to automation runbooks. All rollback actions must log to Audit (Console) and create follow-up ticket for root-cause analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PRD reviewed and approved by PM, Eng lead (Serve Runtime), AI SRE, and Design for Console UX; 2) Sampling matrix documented with example sample extracts and tagging schema; 3) Threshold formulas and statistical methods documented with worked examples and sensitivity analysis; 4) A/B spec includes sample size calculators and pre-registered hypothesis template; 5) Rollback playbook includes automation hooks and notification templates; 6) Demo: run the eval pipeline on archived traffic and show a synthetic regression that correctly triggers soft-warning then hard-fail and results in a simulated rollback. Approval indicated in Confluence link.
updates: 2025-02-12: Scoped draft produced and shared with ENG; flagged question about baseline window length — ENG prefers 14 days for throughput cost, PM prefers 28 days for stability.
2025-02-18: AI SRE suggested adding sustained-deviation requirement (3 consecutive windows) to reduce flapping; incorporated into regression_thresholds.

2025-02-24: Data team provided variance estimates for core metric; updated sample size guidance and MDE assumptions. Added Benjamini-Hochberg as preferred FDR control for multi-metric checks per statistics review.
2025-03-02: Console design reviewed initial alert UX; added explicit audit log requirement and rollback confirmation modal; design requested copy edits — assigned to UX writer.
2025-03-04: PM review complete; moved to In Progress with engineering sub-issues created for pipeline hooks and Console UI changes.
reviewer_feedback: Luca Moretti (Eng): Concern about cost of traffic-proportional sampling at 70% — proposed progressive sampling where we downsample common tokens while preserving route diversity.
Marta Rodriguez (AI SRE): Add immediate safety escalation path that bypasses statistical thresholds when a class of high-severity safety signals appear.
Evan Chen (Data Scientist): Recommend adding holdout baseline to estimate false-positive rate and calibrate thresholds monthly.
Samira Khan (Design): Request to expose a compact summary card in Console showing composite quality delta + reason codes for rollbacks to reduce triage time.
